Carrier says some still unable to connect to emergency hotline a day after initial mobile network outage Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Telstra customers are still having trouble calling triple zero on Thursday morning as the telecommunications giant confirmed a secondary issue stemming from Wednesday’s national outage continued to impact calls. Some who tried to call the emergency hotline were receiving an error message and their phones would try to connect to an alternative network, Telstra said. Customers have been urged to wait for the phone to connect to another network, or use a different device to make their call.

Telstra CFO Michael Ackman said on Wednesday morning that 90 per cent of the issues had been resolved, but the telco advised: “It may take some time for all devices to reconnect correctly.” It later identified a “secondary issue” was affecting Triple-0 calls. For customers still impacted by this, Telstra warns that an error message will appear on the device, which will try to connect to an alternative mobile network. It advised customers to wait up to 90 seconds for this to happen, and use a different phone to make the emergency call if an alternative network could not be reached. If you’d like to view this content, please adjust your . To find out more about how we use cookies, please see our Cookie Guide. The Australian Rail Track Corporation (ARTC) is still being affected by the Telstra outage.

The federal communications minister, Anika Wells, told ABC radio: “In some instances calls are going straight to message bank. In some instances, 000 calls were not going through. “It has been largely resolved, but there are still residual problems,” she said. In a statement early Thursday, Telstra said: “We’re deeply sorry for the impact this issue has had on so many people.” As of 6.30am on Thursday morning, Telstra said the occurrence of the secondary triple-zero issue had been reduced by 90%. But the minister for industry, Tim Ayres, told the ABC on Thursday that “100% is the only acceptable figure here”. The telco’s issues have continued to wreak havoc across Australia. All the trains on Victoria’s regional rail network were still suspended on Thursday morning, up to and including the morning peak travel period.

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Carrier says some still unable to connect to emergency hotline a day after initial mobile network outage

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Telstra customers are still having trouble calling triple zero on Thursday morning as the telecommunications giant confirmed a secondary issue stemming from Wednesday’s national outage continued to impact calls.

Some who tried to call the emergency hotline were receiving an error message and their phones would try to connect to an alternative network, Telstra said.

Customers have been urged to wait for the phone to connect to another network, or use a different device to make their call.

The federal communications minister, Anika Wells, told ABC radio: “In some instances calls are going straight to message bank. In some instances, 000 calls were not going through.

“It has been largely resolved, but there are still residual problems,” she said.

In a statement early Thursday, Telstra said: “We’re deeply sorry for the impact this issue has had on so many people.”

As of 6.30am on Thursday morning, Telstra said the occurrence of the secondary triple-zero issue had been reduced by 90%.

But the minister for industry, Tim Ayres, told the ABC on Thursday that “100% is the only acceptable figure here”.

The telco’s issues have continued to wreak havoc across Australia.

All the trains on Victoria’s regional rail network were still suspended on Thursday morning, up to and including the morning peak travel period.

“The V/Line network continues to be impacted following the nationwide Telstra telecommunications outage, with passenger services unable to operate,” V/Line said in a statement on its website.

Wells said she had not yet heard of any “adverse outcomes” linked to the continuing triple-zero issues as Ayres revealed there would be a full investigation into the outages.

“Communications and digital infrastructure [are] part of the lifeblood of the economy,” he said.

“Each of these operators has responsibilities here.

“The framework is there to manage those, to make sure we’ve got a transparent investigative framework and to apply penalties where it’s necessary.”

Thousands of customers were unable to make calls or access data on Wednesday after a software defect affected Telstra’s systems, the telco said.

The company made more than 300 welfare checks to people who attempted to dial triple zero during the episode.

The Australian Rail Track Corporation (ARTC) is still being affected by the Telstra outage.

The ARTC train communication system — which allows network control centres to communicate directly with train drivers — was disrupted on Wednesday.

The in-cab radio system operates over Telstra’s 4G network.

The Telstra outage stopped the ARTC “from making or receiving essential communications with train crews and frontline workers, posing a safety risk,” it said on Thursday.

payload.title: Telstran häiriöt vaikeuttivat hätäpuheluja Australiassa
payload.summary: Australian Telstran verkko-ongelmat jatkuivat torstaina, kun yhtiö kertoi hätäpuheluihin vaikuttaneesta toissijaisesta häiriöstä. Osa asiakkaista ei saanut yhteyttä triple zero -hätänumeroon, ja Victorian aluejunaliikenne pysyi keskeytettynä.
payload.content:
Australian teleoperaattori Telstran häiriöt jatkuivat torstaiaamuna sen jälkeen, kun keskiviikon valtakunnallisen mobiiliverkon vian jäljiltä havaittiin uusi ongelma, joka vaikeutti yhteyden saamista maan triple zero -hätänumeroon. Yhtiön mukaan osa asiakkaista sai puhelimeensa virheilmoituksen, minkä jälkeen laite yritti yhdistää vaihtoehtoiseen mobiiliverkkoon.

## Hätäpuheluissa oli yhä jäännösongelmia

Telstra kertoi, että niin sanotun toissijaisen triple zero -ongelman esiintyminen oli vähentynyt 90 prosentilla torstaiaamuun kello 6.30 mennessä. Häiriö ei kuitenkaan ollut kokonaan ohi. Liittovaltion viestintäministeri Anika Wells sanoi ABC-radiolle, että joissakin tapauksissa puhelut menivät suoraan vastaajaan ja joissakin tapauksissa 000-puhelut eivät menneet läpi. Hänen mukaansa tilanne oli suurelta osin korjattu, mutta jälkiongelmia oli edelleen.

Yhtiö ohjeisti asiakkaita odottamaan, että puhelin yhdistää toiseen verkkoon. Lähteiden mukaan yhdistymistä voi joutua odottamaan enintään 90 sekuntia. Jos vaihtoehtoista verkkoa ei saada käyttöön, hätäpuhelu kehotettiin tekemään toisella puhelimella.

## Telstra pahoitteli vaikutuksia

Telstra pahoitteli varhain torstaina antamassaan lausunnossa häiriön vaikutuksia moniin ihmisiin. Yhtiön talousjohtaja Michael Ackman oli sanonut keskiviikkoaamuna, että 90 prosenttia ongelmista oli ratkaistu, mutta Telstra varoitti jo tuolloin, että kaikkien laitteiden uudelleenyhdistyminen voi kestää.

Teollisuusministeri Tim Ayres korosti ABC:lle, että hätäpuhelujen osalta vain täysi toimintavarmuus on hyväksyttävä taso. Hänen mukaansa 100 prosenttia on ainoa hyväksyttävä luku tilanteessa, jossa kyse on hätänumeroon pääsystä.

## Junaliikenne pysyi poikki Victoriassa

Häiriöt vaikuttivat myös liikenteeseen. Australian Rail Track Corporationin kerrottiin kärsivän edelleen Telstran katkosta, ja Victorian alueellinen junaverkko oli torstaiaamuna yhä kokonaan keskeytettynä. Keskeytys jatkui lähdetietojen mukaan myös aamun ruuhkahuipun ajan.
summary_bullets: Telstran mobiiliverkon häiriön jälkiongelma vaikeutti yhteyksiä Australian triple zero -hätänumeroon.
Yhtiö kehotti odottamaan vaihtoehtoiseen verkkoon yhdistymistä tai käyttämään toista puhelinta.
Victorian alueellinen junaliikenne oli torstaiaamuna yhä keskeytettynä.
